title: Java Errors and Compiler Diagnostics
learningObjectives: Classify syntax, compile-time, runtime and logic errors

understand.concept: A syntax or type error prevents compilation; a runtime exception interrupts execution; a logic error produces an incorrect result. Read the first useful compiler diagnostic, inspect its source location and nearby code, make one correction, then compile again.
understand.whyItMatters: Java Errors and Compiler Diagnostics helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain. It connects core language knowledge with realistic programming tasks.
understand.analogy: Treat this concept as a clearly labeled tool: select it for a specific responsibility and check the result.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a learning aid; actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Java Errors and Compiler Diagnostics

A syntax or type error prevents compilation; a runtime exception interrupts execution; a logic error produces an incorrect result. Read the first useful compiler diagnostic, inspect its source location and nearby code, make one correction, then compile again.

## Applying the concept

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that directly supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failure cases and state assumptions clearly.

## Verification checklist

- Compile with JDK 21.
- Predict the output before running.
- Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Check resource cleanup and error handling.
- Prefer explicit types and focused methods.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int value = Integer.parseInt("42"); System.out.println(value); } }
examples.explanation: Shows a valid conversion; contrast it with a NumberFormatException at runtime.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String source = "Main.java"; int line = 7; System.out.println(source + ":" + line + ": error: cannot find symbol"); } }
examples.explanation: Illustrates the shape of a compiler diagnostic: file, line and message.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int expected = 10; int actual = 8 + 2; System.out.println(expected == actual); } }
examples.explanation: Compares expected and actual results to detect a logic defect.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try { Integer.parseInt("four"); } catch (NumberFormatException ex) { System.out.println(ex.getClass().getSimpleName()); } } }
examples.explanation: Demonstrates a runtime exception rather than a compile-time diagnostic.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int divisor = 0; System.out.println(divisor == 0 ? "Check divisor before division" : 10 / divisor); } }
examples.explanation: Shows input validation preventing a runtime arithmetic failure.

practise.guidedTask: Create three tiny Java files: one with a syntax error, one with a runtime parse failure, and one with an incorrect calculation. Compile/run each and record how the failure differs.
practise.independentTask: Repair a supplied broken calculator. Keep a short defect log with the compiler/runtime message, source location, root cause, correction and regression test.
hints: State the input, output and assumptions before coding.
Use the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior.
Predict the result, compile with JDK 21, then test a boundary or failure case.
practise.challenge: Try an invalid numeric string and a zero divisor. Explain which failures javac catches and which require runtime validation.
